outcomes: Explain an identity shortcut and trace its gradient
Normalize an image with explicit mean, variance, and epsilon
Generate label-preserving translations without crossing split boundaries
Train two small pre-normalized residual convolutional blocks
lessons: Why deeper stacks become hard to optimize

residual-connection.name: residual connection
residual-connection.definition: A shortcut that adds a block input to a learned transformation of that input.
residual-connection.explanation: A residual block computes y = x + F(x), usually followed or preceded by a nonlinearity and normalization. The identity path carries the input forward without learned weights and contributes a direct term to the backward gradient. The branch can focus on a correction rather than reconstructing the whole signal. Shapes must match for elementwise addition; projection shortcuts are needed when channel count or spatial resolution changes.

normalization.name: normalization
normalization.definition: A transformation that centers and scales values using explicit statistics.
normalization.explanation: Normalization subtracts a mean and divides by a standard deviation, usually with a small epsilon inside the square root. Which axes supply the statistics defines the method. Batch normalization uses mini-batch statistics during training and stored running statistics at inference. The chapter project uses per-image statistics so its tiny deterministic batches need no running state. This changes the method and is stated explicitly; it still exposes the numerical purpose and boundary conditions.

data-augmentation.name: data augmentation
data-augmentation.definition: A label-preserving transformation used to create additional training views.
data-augmentation.explanation: Image translations, crops, flips, color changes, and distortions can teach invariance when they preserve the intended label. The validity of a transform depends on the task: a horizontal flip may preserve a cat label but change the meaning of text or traffic signs. Augmentation belongs inside the training pipeline after splitting. Creating variants before splitting can put near-duplicates in training and validation and produce an optimistic evaluation.

identity-shortcut.name: identity shortcut
identity-shortcut.definition: A parameter-free route that copies a block input into its output sum.
identity-shortcut.explanation: When input and output shapes agree, an identity shortcut simply adds each input element to the corresponding residual-branch element. Its derivative with respect to the input contains an exact one, plus any contribution through the branch. This route helps information and gradients cross a block. It does not guarantee that every deep network trains well; optimization also depends on initialization, normalization, nonlinearities, data, and learning rate.

invariance.name: invariance
invariance.definition: Insensitivity of a prediction or representation to a specified transformation.
invariance.explanation: A classifier is invariant to a transformation when its output remains useful after that transformation, such as a small translation of an object. Convolution shares a detector across locations, pooling reduces sensitivity locally, and augmentation supplies examples of acceptable changes. Invariance must be chosen, not assumed. Excessive translation can crop away evidence, and transformations that alter the label teach contradictory targets. Measure performance on held-out transformed examples rather than inferring invariance from architecture alone.

checks: First residual-block kernel analytic and numerical gradients agree through both blocks
Normalized fixture images have mean approximately zero
Training reduces held-out loss and classifies all four canonical images
Augmentation is deterministic and limited to training rows
limitations: The project uses per-image normalization rather than batch normalization
One scalar convolution channel and a small dense head are used
Translations are hand-selected and do not model real camera variation
The four-image held-out set cannot estimate real-world accuracy
